discrepancies.status: UNEXPLAINED. The letter is dated August 3, 2020 (decision). Whether June 30 is a resubmission or additional-information date is NOT VERIFIED.

discrepancies.a: FDA: 11 US study sites (655-subject analysis population)
discrepancies.b: JAMA: 15 US centres (942 consented: 6 primary care, 6 general ophthalmology, 3 retina); registry: 1 location listed
discrepancies.status: Different populations counted (655 analysed versus 942 consented), and the registry list is incomplete. A claim that says 'N sites' must say which count.

discrepancies.a: FDA: 942 consented, 915 eligible, 655 analysed (22 and older)
discrepancies.b: JAMA: 942 consented, 915 eligible, 893 completed (1786 eyes); registry: 942
discrepancies.status: Different analysis populations; no conflict in the funnel's first two steps.

discrepancies.a: FDA analysis population: 22 years and older (subjects 21 or younger excluded)
discrepancies.b: JAMA and registry: 18 years or older (range 18-88); FDA indication: 'adults'
discrepancies.status: Real scope difference: the indicated population is 'adults', the FDA-analysed population is 22 and older, the published population starts at 18. Age 18 to 21 is evidenced by the paper but not by FDA's analysis.

discrepancies.a: FDA: per-cohort eye-level results (for example primary care, enrichment permitted: mtmDR sensitivity 92.9% [87.1-97.5], specificity 85.6%)
discrepancies.status: Different analysis populations and weighting, not a conflict. A claim must name which result it quotes.

discrepancies.field: software version of the pivotal-trial build
discrepancies.a: FDA: silent (v2.1.0 is the cleared device; rev005 and rev006 appear for human-factors work)
discrepancies.b: JAMA abstract: version 2.1.0; registry: frozen build, no number
discrepancies.status: Release string agrees, build identity not stated anywhere. NOT VERIFIED beyond the string.

discrepancies.a: K200667 (v2.1.0): not previously diagnosed with MORE THAN MILD diabetic retinopathy; primary care and eye care named
discrepancies.b: K223357 (v2.2.0): not previously diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy; Topcon NW400 added; no setting sentence
discrepancies.status: The later indication is narrower on prior disease and silent on setting. Evidence for one version cannot be carried to the other without restating the indication.

discrepancies.a: PubMed lists an erratum (PMID 34935926, JAMA Netw Open 2021 Dec 1;4(12):e2144317)
discrepancies.status: What changed in Figure 2 is NOT VERIFIED (the PubMed record has no text). The abstract numbers quoted here were read from the current PubMed record, which postdates the erratum link (record revised 2026-05-18).
The registry was last verified before the results existed and has no publication link.

demo.claimedUseQuestion: Can our primary-care clinics use EyeArt version 2.1.0 to screen adults aged 22 or older who have diabetes and no previous diagnosis of more than mild diabetic retinopathy, and does the evidence behind the vendor's statement that sensitivity for more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy is at least 85 percent apply to that use?

exclusions: previously diagnosed with more than mild diabetic retinopathy

resultsToTestAgainst.note: tiny cohort; point estimate above 85, lower confidence bound below

resultsToTestAgainst.source: FDA Table 3 (enrichment permitted), primary care, 670 eyes

demo.note: Whether the claim is judged on point estimates or on the lower confidence bound is a rule choice with no source threshold; the tiny cohort makes it matter. The date is left out of the base claim: a deployment date after 2020 triggers the staleness rule (no source threshold, REQUIRES_DOMAIN_REVIEW) and belongs in the counterfactual lab.

counterfactuals.expected: evidence for 2.1.0 no longer covers the claimed version; K223357 (2.2.0) is the evidence, with a narrower indication wording
PARTIAL: FDA analysis floor is 22; the paper covers 18 and older
PARTIAL, narrower scope 22 and older (claim EA-02)
DISJOINT with primary care and eye care
K200667 permits it ('more than mild'); K223357 does not (claim EA-05)
REQUIRES_DOMAIN_REVIEW: no staleness window in any source; a successor clearance exists (claim EA-03)

secondPass.method: regex and parsed-JSON re-extraction from raw records plus recomputation of every Table 2/3 cell
secondPass.note: During development the second-pass script reported four disagreements; all four were bugs in the checking code (a regex dropped by shell escaping, an expected-token count, and a rounding convention: FDA prints 37/80 as 46.2%, an exact half rounded down), not differences between the readings. They were fixed and the script re-run to 74 of 74. Two further regexes were found to be vacuous and were repaired; each absence check was then tested against a positive control.
